title: Argument Labels That Read Like English

docs.title: Functions — Function Argument Labels and Parameter Names

hints: Each parameter can have an external label and a different internal name.
The signature is already written — use `start`, `end` and `step` inside the body.
jsBridge: JS has no argument labels; you pass an options object `{from, to, by}` to get readable calls. Swift builds labels into the signature: `move(from:to:by:)` is the function's **name**. The external label (`from`) and internal name (`start`) can differ.

compass.q: An options object `{from, to}` vs Swift labels: which one lets you reorder arguments? Which one is checked at compile time?
Read Apple's API Design Guidelines on labels. Why is it `insert(_:at:)` and not `insert(element:atIndex:)`?
Can two functions differ only by labels, like `move(from:to:)` and `move(start:end:)`? Is that overloading?
Java has no labels, so builder patterns became popular. Do Swift labels reduce the need for builders?
